description: HIMS in-patient discharge process. Logical schema only -- physical layout (partitioning, ordering, evolution) lives in table-config.json.

hims_employees.description: Staff master data. Replicated as a full-table snapshot each day; no incremental key exists in the source.

columns.name: role
columns.doc: doctor | nurse-staff | nurse-mgr | pharma-mgr | billing-mgr | transport-staff | evs-staff

hims_discharge.description: One row per discharge process instance. Updated in place as the process advances; a cancelled discharge is restarted the next day under the same process_id.

columns.name: process_type
columns.doc: Constant 'discharge'. Present so the table can later hold other process types.

columns.name: process_id
columns.doc: = discharge_id. UUIDv7, so it is time-ordered.

columns.name: status
columns.doc: pending | initiated | nurse_cleared | pharma_cleared | billing_pending | billing_cleared | cancelled | discharged. 'discharged' is terminal -- EVS events continue against it.

columns.name: room_id
columns.doc: Bed the patient occupies; the room EVS later cleans.

columns.name: scheduled_at
columns.doc: Planned departure. Null for unplanned discharges.

columns.name: created_at
columns.doc: When the row first appeared. Stable for the row's life, which is why it is the partition key.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.doc: Replication key. Moves on every status change, including a next-day restart.

hims_events.description: Discharge process event stream. See HIMS_Discharge_Process_Events.md for the event catalogue.

columns.name: actor_id
columns.doc: -> hims_employees.employee_id. Null for system-generated events such as bed_cleaning_required.

columns.name: process_type
columns.doc: Added beyond the original brief: needed as a column so events can be partitioned and z-ordered by the process they belong to.

columns.name: process_id
columns.doc: -> hims_discharge.process_id. Added beyond the original brief for the same reason.

columns.name: data
columns.doc: Event-specific properties as JSON text. VARCHAR rather than VARIANT because PyIceberg 0.11.1 has no VariantType.
